Cell-Level Gene-Protein Coupling Analysis

Source: R/cell-coupling.R
run_cell_coupling.Rd

Computes within-donor Spearman partial correlations between gene expression and protein abundance at the single-cell level, then uses random-effects meta-regression to test whether coupling strength varies with a donor-level exposure.

Usage

run_cell_coupling(
  x,
  genes,
  proteins,
  exposure,
  celltype,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  altexp_name = "CITE",
  confounders = NULL,
  min_cells = 30L,
  min_donors = 10L,
  meta_moderators = NULL,
  var_method = c("asymptotic", "bootstrap"),
  n_boot = 200L
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment object. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x). Must contain an altExp named altexp_name with cell-level protein counts.

genes

Character vector of gene names to test.

proteins

Character vector of protein names to test (must be present in altExp).

exposure

Character; name of the exposure variable in exposureData(x).

celltype

Character; cell type to analyse.

celltype_col

Character; column in colData containing cell type labels. Default "cell_type".

altexp_name

Character; name of the altExp containing protein data. Default "CITE".

confounders

Character vector of column names in colData(x) to partial out (e.g., c("S.Score", "G2M.Score", "percent.mt")). Library sizes (nCount_RNA, nCount_protein) are always controlled regardless of this parameter. Each confounder is ranked within a donor, so it must be numeric, logical, an ordered factor or a label with at most two values; an unordered label with more categories, such as a cell-cycle phase, is an error and must be given as 0/1 indicator columns for all its categories but one, leaving out a category that every donor has cells of (for G1, S and G2M, for example S and G2M when every donor has G1 cells). The names gene, protein, lib_rna and lib_prot are used for the variables of the partial correlation and cannot be confounder names. Nor can a confounder be a column that is not passed on as one column under its own name: a matrix or nested table with several columns or with a column name other than that of the confounder, or a column with the name of an argument of data.frame (row.names, check.rows, check.names, fix.empty.names or stringsAsFactors). Default NULL (library sizes only).

min_cells

Integer; minimum cells per donor to include. Default 30.

min_donors

Integer; minimum number of donors with enough cells (at least min_cells, and at least 7 plus the number of confounders, because the two library sizes are always adjusted for) and values of the exposure and of every moderator. A gene-protein pair also needs a partial correlation in that many donors. Default 10.

meta_moderators

Character vector or one-sided formula of additional donor-level moderators for the meta-regression (e.g., "age", c("age", "sex") or ~ age + sex). These must be columns in exposureData(x) with syntactic R names (see make.names) other than ., ... and names such as ..1, which R reads specially in a formula; a formula may only list such columns, without transformations or interactions. The exposure itself cannot be a moderator, and the names yi, vi, donor_exp, intrcpt and meta_formula, which the meta-regression uses for its own variables, cannot be moderator names. Default NULL (exposure only).

var_method

Character. Method for estimating the sampling variance of Fisher z-transformed correlations. "asymptotic" (default) uses the formula \(1.06 / (n - q - 3)\). "bootstrap" resamples cells within each donor to compute empirical variance, which is more accurate for small cell counts or non-normal data but slower. The bootstrap uses the random number generator, so set a seed for reproducible variances.

n_boot

Integer. Number of bootstrap replicates per donor when var_method = "bootstrap". Default 200.

Value

A DataFrame with one row per gene-protein pair (zero rows when too few donors qualify). A pair whose exposure does not vary among its donors, or is collinear with the moderators, is not tested, with a warning that counts such pairs:

gene, protein

Feature names.

n_donors

Number of donors in the meta-regression: donors with enough cells, a partial correlation and values of the exposure and of every moderator.

beta0, se0, pval0

Intercept (baseline coupling).

beta1, se1, pval1

Exposure coefficient: the slope, across donors, of the Fisher z of the coupling on the exposure.

tau2

Between-donor heterogeneity variance (REML).

I2

Heterogeneity percentage.

mean_r

Mean partial correlation across donors.

mean_n_cells

Mean cells per donor.

n_confounders

Number of conditioning variables requested (library sizes plus confounders); variables constant within a donor are dropped for that donor.

Details

For each gene-protein pair, the method proceeds in two stages:

Stage 1 (within-donor): For each donor \(d\) with at least min_cells cells of the specified cell type, compute the Spearman partial correlation between gene expression and protein abundance, controlling for library sizes and any user-specified confounders: $$r_d = \rho_S(\text{gene}_i, \text{protein}_j \mid \text{nCount\_RNA}, \text{nCount\_protein}, \text{confounders})$$ Then apply Fisher's z-transform: $$z_d = \text{arctanh}(r_d), \quad \text{Var}(z_d) \approx 1.06 / (n_d - q - 3)$$ where \(q\) is the number of conditioning variables (2 + length of confounders, less any that are constant within the donor and therefore dropped). The factor 1.06 corrects for the efficiency loss of rank-based correlation (Fieller et al. 1957).

Stage 2 (across-donor meta-regression): Fit a random-effects model via REML with Knapp-Hartung adjustment: $$z_d = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{exposure}_d + \sum_k \gamma_k \cdot \text{moderator}_{dk} + u_d + \varepsilon_d$$ where \(\varepsilon_d \sim N(0, v_d)\) (known sampling variance) and \(u_d \sim N(0, \tau^2)\) (between-donor heterogeneity). The Knapp-Hartung adjustment provides more accurate confidence intervals for small numbers of studies (donors), using a t-distribution with \(D - p - 1\) degrees of freedom rather than a z-distribution.

Confounder control: Cell-level confounders (cell cycle, mitochondrial content, ambient RNA scores) are partialed out in Stage 1, ensuring that the correlation reflects genuine gene-protein coupling rather than shared technical or biological confounds. Donor-level moderators (age, sex) are included in Stage 2.

References

Viechtbauer W (2010). Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor package. J Stat Softw, 36(3), 1-48. doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03

Fieller EC, Hartley HO, Pearson ES (1957). Tests for rank correlation coefficients. I. Biometrika, 44, 470-481.

Kim S (2015). ppcor: An R Package for a Fast Calculation to Semi-partial Correlation Coefficients. Commun Stat Appl Methods, 22(6), 665-674.

Examples

set.seed(1)
donors <- sprintf("D%02d", 1:12)
donor <- rep(donors, each = 60)
gene <- matrix(stats::rpois(2 * length(donor), 10), nrow = 2,
    dimnames = list(c("Gene1", "Gene2"), paste0("c", seq_along(donor))))
protein <- matrix(stats::rpois(2 * length(donor), 5), nrow = 2,
    dimnames = list(c("Prot1", "Prot2"), colnames(gene)))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = gene),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(donor_id = donor, cell_type = "T"))
SingleCellExperiment::altExp(sce, "CITE") <-
    SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
        assays = list(counts = protein))
exp_mat <- matrix(seq(0, 2, length.out = 12), ncol = 1,
    dimnames = list(donors, "exposure"))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
if (requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ppcor", quietly = TRUE)) {
    run_cell_coupling(scee, genes = "Gene1", proteins = "Prot1",
        exposure = "exposure", celltype = "T",
        min_cells = 20L, min_donors = 10L)
}
#> [exposomeSC] Cell coupling: T, 1 genes x 1 proteins = 1 pairs, 2 confounders
#> [exposomeSC] 1 pairs tested for T
